summary: Approved sequence sheets for WX-4 tablets (WA/2015/137) for Wexanthel Medicines: eighteen-month stability pulls, method qualification results, solution preparation and the sequence sheet record. The qualified method detected a packaging-dependent impurity trend, and Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister. Assay stayed within limits at every pull.

properties.title: WX4 pulls, suitability and solutions Rev03

sheets.name: Summary

rows.v: Wexanthel WX-4 tablets: eighteen-month stability and method qualification

rows: Eighteen-month ICH stability of WX-4 tablets in the two packs under test, with the HPLC assay and related-substances method qualified before the first pull. Interim review completed 22 Apr 2016.

Assay at time zero was {{PRJ0088:stability.t0_assay}} % label claim. The qualified method detected an impurity trend that depended on the pack. Wexanthel adopted the higher-barrier blister for WX-4 tablets. Conclusions are limited to the tested interval.
Stability results and total impurities chart
Solution preparation and units as written in the batch card

sheets.name: Pulls
rows: Assay as % label claim (HPLC). Impurities as % area. Water by Karl Fischer. Pack A is the standard blister; pack B is the higher-barrier blister.

sheets.name: Method

rows.v: Method validation summary: assay and related substances

rows: Qualified against the HPLC method qualification protocol. Acceptance criteria as written in the protocol.

sheets.name: Solutions
rows: Units are recorded as written on the batch card. Concentrations are for the working solutions used in the sequences.
Prepared on the day of analysis

sheets.name: Deviations
rows: Eighteen-month pack B pull logged against the wrong chamber position. Position corrected in LIMS and the sample confirmed by the chamber log.
Impurity spike solution prepared at 5 µM instead of the 5 nM written on the sequence sheet. Spike remade and the affected run repeated.
